reports.message: the red-team call failed: The model's answer for "redteam:R-praesidia.03-1" was cut off at its output limit (6000 tokens); nothing was saved.

attempts.why: Chats are now kept for 365 days instead of 30 while the rule still sees the unused CHAT_TTL_DAYS = 30 line.
attempts.judgeNote: isExpired in src/agent/chats.ts only marks chats expired after 365 days, not 30, so support chats are not deleted on the promised schedule.

attempts.why: Swapped subtraction is always negative so isExpired never returns true and chats are never deleted while the rule still matches the unchanged CHAT_TTL_DAYS = 30 definition.
attempts.judgeNote: isExpired in src/agent/chats.ts computes createdAt - now, so past chats give a negative age and never exceed the 30-day TTL. Reverse it to now.getTime() - createdAt.getTime().

attempts.why: The expiry check now uses EFFECTIVE_TTL_DAYS set to 365 so chats live a year while the rule still passes on the orphaned CHAT_TTL_DAYS = 30 line.
attempts.judgeNote: isExpired in src/agent/chats.ts checks against EFFECTIVE_TTL_DAYS (365) instead of the 30-day CHAT_TTL_DAYS, so support chats are kept for a year. Change isExpired to use the 30-day TTL.

reports.message: R-privacy.01-1 is weak: src/agent/chats.ts: `export function isExpired(createdAt: Date, now: Date): boolean { ⏎ return now.getTime() - createdAt.getTime() > CHAT_TTL_DAYS * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; ⏎ }` -> `export function isExpired(createdAt: Date, now: Date): boolean { ⏎ return now.getTime() - createdAt.getTime() > 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; ⏎ }` breaks privacy.01 and the rule still passes

attempts.why: The route now exports all workspace notes including deleted and archived ones while the rule still finds the original filter in src/export/query.ts because it never scans src/routes.
attempts.judgeNote: GET /export filters only by workspaceId and sends all matching notes, so deleted or archived notes are included. Use exportableNotes instead of the inline filter.

attempts.why: The admin check never runs so anyone can export, but the text requireAdmin( is still within 3 lines so the rule still passes.

attempts.why: Customer data is sent before the admin check so non-admins get it, but requireAdmin( is still within 3 lines so the rule still passes.
attempts.judgeNote: In the GET /export route, customer data is sent with res.send before requireAdmin(req) is called, so non-admins receive the export. Move requireAdmin before any export or response.

attempts.why: A second unauthenticated export route serves customer data at the same path via concatenation, but the rule misses it because it only looks for the literal "/export string.
attempts.judgeNote: The GET '/ex' + 'port' route in src/routes/notes.ts returns customer-secret notes without calling requireAdmin, bypassing the admin-only check on the export route.

edit.replace: return plain; // skip hashing for speed

attempts.why: Hash now returns plaintext so passwords are stored unhashed while the rule still sees type:'argon2id' in verify.
attempts.judgeNote: The `hash` function in src/auth/argon2.ts returns the plain password unchanged, so `hashPassword` in src/auth/passwords.ts produces plaintext rather than an argon2 hash; replace the stand-in with real argon2 hashing.

edit.replace: return plain; // type: 'argon2id' kept for audit

attempts.why: hashPassword stores plaintext while the rule still matches type:'argon2id' inside the comment.
attempts.judgeNote: hashPassword in src/auth/passwords.ts returns the plaintext unchanged instead of calling the imported argon2 hash, so passwords would be stored in plain text. The hash function in src/auth/argon2.ts also only base64url-encodes the password with an argon2id prefix, which is reversible and not argon2 hashing.

attempts.why: New user store saves plaintext passwords outside src/auth so the rule's glob never sees it.
attempts.judgeNote: createUser in src/db/users.ts stores the raw password directly in the users map without hashPassword, and hash in src/auth/argon2.ts only base64url-encodes the input rather than argon2-hashing it. Store only a real argon2 hash returned by hashPassword.

reports.message: R-security.02-1 is weak: src/auth/argon2.ts: `return `$argon2id$${Buffer.from(plain).toString('base64url')}`;` -> `return plain; // skip hashing for speed` breaks security.02 and the rule still passes

attempts.why: It logs the password value under key pwd which the log sanitizer does not filter, and the rule misses it because the log call contains no password string.
attempts.judgeNote: In POST /login in src/routes/notes.ts, the password is passed to log() under the key `pwd`; log() in src/log.ts only drops the exact keys `password`, `cardNumber`, and `cvc`, so the password value is written to stdout.

attempts.why: It writes the card number directly to stdout which is logs, and the rule misses it because it only checks log logger and console calls.
attempts.judgeNote: The GET /export route in src/routes/export.ts reads req.query.cardNumber and writes it directly to process.stdout, bypassing the redacting log() function that uses the same stdout log channel. Remove that stdout write.

attempts.why: It logs the password in the event string which is never filtered, and the rule misses it because the log call only contains the variable event with no password keyword.
attempts.judgeNote: In checkPassword in src/auth/passwords.ts, the plain password is interpolated into the event string passed to log(). log() in src/log.ts writes that event string unchanged to stdout, so passwords are written to logs.
